No uninterrupted all-crossing operation or all-person continuity is inferred.

EA003-D1 — Reported road restrictions and observed scoped reopening
Ordinary road-passenger service at Zamiin Uud–Erenhot, to the first resumed passenger coach.
Exact first operational interruption: not established. Reuters reports national road restrictions from 2020-01-27; a contemporary Montsame account dates selective road restrictions to 2020-01-28, with permitted cohorts. February 1 rules further changed nationality and direction conditions.
Observed scoped reopening: 2023-01-08.
Exact complete operational duration withheld because the first service interruption is unresolved. The municipal-government reopening account describes a three-year suspension of this road-passenger channel, supporting a duration greater than 24 hours without validating the 1,077-day total.

phases.Movement / crossing / phase scope: Ordinary road-passenger service at Zamiin Uud–Erenhot, to the first resumed passenger coach.
phases.Qualification:
EA003-D1: The national January 27 report is retained as reported chronology, not an independently established first interruption of every ordinary road-passenger service at Zamiin Uud. Montsame-derived accounts date selective road restrictions to January 28 and still permit specified business/transit Mongolians and foreign travellers. The February 1 embassy rules further distinguish foreign entry, citizens' returns and freight. These changing cohorts prevent treating January 27–January 8, 2023 as a verified complete 1,077-day operational spell. January 8 remains the observed first resumed passenger-coach endpoint. A municipal-government report describes the road-passenger channel as suspended for three years, supporting greater-than-24-hour eligibility independently of the unresolved exact onset. Other posts and rail services have separate histories; NIA and People's Daily share one reporting origin.

REC50-R11-EA003-P1: The regional Erenhot–Ulaanbaatar suspension is reported from 14 February 2020 and the first inbound return is observed on 30 August 2023. Those dates differ by 1,293 days, while a CCTV account reports a 1,295-day pause. Numeric duration is withheld pending reconciliation; the January road endpoint is unchanged. The Beijing train has a different suspension date; earlier nationality-specific ticket limits and the future two-way timetable are distinct. This adds evidence to the existing parent rather than creating another parent.

Rail duration and temporal anchor: Reconcile the 1,295-day reported passenger-train pause with the 1,293-day difference between the separately reported dates; preserve the regional route and first inbound-return scope.

Goods and local travellers.
Direction: Chinese exports to Myanmar and Myanmar residents seeking visits or treatment in China; commodity exemptions are asymmetric.
Exceptions: Tissue-culture bananas and rare-earth exports to China continued selectively. October 2025 reopening reports cover food, construction materials and some visits/medical treatment, while fuel and electronics remained restricted at that time. phases.Qualification: EA011-D1: Crossing-specific reporting dates Laiza closure October 18, 2024; RFA broadly says October 19. Reopening reports disagree: KIO spokesperson quoted by Myitkyina Journal gives October 24 at 23:59, Irrawaddy reports Saturday October 25, and Mizzima gives October 26. Preserve October 24–26 as a reported endpoint range rather than choosing one exact day. December 13, 2024 removal of Laiza barriers did not establish passage: contemporary KNG reporting explicitly says people, vehicles and goods were still not allowed. Kan Paik Ti had separate earlier partial reopening. These reports do not independently establish uninterrupted closure for all categories or every Kachin crossing. The October fuel restriction is not a current-status assertion: Network Media Group reported limited fuel tankers entering Laiza–Nabang by November 26, 2025, but first passage, retail availability and full policy repeal remain unknown.

phases.Movement: ordinary passengers
phases.Movement / crossing / phase scope: Malaysian land-entry restrictions on foreign visitors and outward social travel by Malaysians/permanent residents
phases.Qualification:
EA013-R1: The March 18–31 2020 original order is a scheduled window; March 31 does not signify actual reopening. Freight, returns, diplomats and authorised categories were excepted; transit across Brunei remained subject to state rules.

EA013-C7P1: The April 1–14 extension is an announced window. The domestic MCO chronology does not establish identical conditions at every land post or an April 14 physical reopening.

EA013-C7P2: The embassy notice of May 15, 2020 confirms the selected admission restrictions. Ordinary foreign-passport holders could leave but not re-enter; expatriate, student, dependent, temporary-work and MM2H pass holders were generally barred, with case-by-case approval for essential-service expatriates. Returning diplomats and eligible family/resident categories were excepted, while domestic helpers required approval. Start and category-specific end remain unknown. Airport quarantine references do not establish land-post implementation. The later April 1, 2022 national admission restoration is an outer bound, not proof of unchanged restrictions in between.

EA013-C7P3: The June 10–August 31 2020 RMCO envelope includes conditional approvals and changing categories. Neither August 31 physical reopening nor an uninterrupted universal passenger ban is inferred.

EA013-C7P4: The August 10 MYEntry announcement documents a category-based permission regime, not a new closure or identical requirements for every expatriate. Malaysia’s Immigration Department confirms discontinuation of MyTravel Pass from April 1 2022; this bounds the pandemic permission restriction without dating every earlier category amendment.

Actual April 1 2022 access is directly confirmed at Woodlands and Tuas for fully vaccinated travellers. Earlier limited travel corridors and changing eligibility remain exceptions. The first reopening at every Thai, Indonesian and Bruneian land post and exact legal amendment sequence are not established. No continuous operational duration is added.

phases.Movement / crossing / phase scope: Open Myanmar border checkpoints with neighbouring countries: national suspension of ordinary foreign entry.
phases.Qualification:
The Ministry of Information explicitly gives March 19, 2020 as the policy start; the Foreign Ministry notice supports foreign-entry scope and local border-population exceptions. This is a formal effective date, not observation at every gate.

Eleven Media reports passport and visa passage at Kawthoung–Ranong from March 7, 2023, including third-country visitors. The blanket suspension therefore no longer described all Myanmar border checkpoints by that date. A nationwide repeal and complete operational chronology remain unknown. Do not infer uninterrupted nationwide closure between these dates.

The official eVisa FAQ lists Kawthaung as an eligible entry point. September 2026 state reporting distinguishes Tachilek’s subsequent June 2023 scam-control restriction from qualified package-tour access. Those narrower regimes are not continuation of the original COVID blanket suspension.

A tour operator’s firsthand account also documents crossing the Mae Sai–Tachileik Friendship Bridge on March 10, 2023 using a passport and day-entry permit. This establishes limited visitor access at that land bridge by that date; it does not establish ordinary visa access nationwide, the first reopening day or repeal of the March 2020 notice.

Start: 2023-10-01 to 2023-10-27.

Later goods evidence: SHAN’s 2025-03-24 report describes coal shipments from Myanmar to China through Chinshwehaw. It also reports Chinese permission for coal, sugarcane and corn imports from November 2024, while its opening paragraph dates coal movement from September 2024. Because these retrospective dates differ, 2025-03-24 is used only as a conservative later bound for some outgoing goods, not as the exact reopening day. This does not prove restoration of Chinese exports to Myanmar, all cargo categories, passenger movement or uninterrupted access. Distinct later China-side restrictions must not be merged with the October 2023–March 2024 post-availability phase.

phases.Movement / crossing / phase scope: Availability of Chinshwehaw commercial border-post services; endpoint is restored permission and post operation, not observed goods flow
phases.Qualification:
R5-EA-003-D1: October 1–27, 2023 onset bounds and the March 11, 2024 post-availability endpoint remain. SHAN residents and MNDAA confirm the office/post reopened March 11; Irrawaddy March 15 says no trade flowed because the junta blocked the Lashio road. Reported absence of recorded trade in April 1–May 17 is a later commercial observation, not proof that the gate itself stayed shut. The exact first restored cargo movement is unresolved. RFA’s December 2023 report mixes Kyin San Kyawt and Chinshwehaw geography, so that named-gate detail is not adopted.

Later goods evidence: SHAN’s 2025-03-24 report describes coal shipments from Myanmar to China through Chinshwehaw. It also reports Chinese permission for coal, sugarcane and corn imports from November 2024, while its opening paragraph dates coal movement from September 2024. Because these retrospective dates differ, 2025-03-24 is used only as a conservative later bound for some outgoing goods, not as the exact reopening day. This does not prove restoration of Chinese exports to Myanmar, all cargo categories, passenger movement or uninterrupted access. Distinct later China-side restrictions must not be merged with the October 2023–March 2024 post-availability phase.

A contemporary October 27, 2023 DMG report quotes a Chinshwehaw resident that the Chinese border crossing was already closed. This narrows the latest possible onset to October 27, but does not establish the first closure hour or replace the March 11 post-availability endpoint with an observed cargo restart.

phases.Movement / crossing / phase scope: Chi Ma–Ai Diem bilateral freight clearance
phases.Qualification:
R6-EA-005-FU1: Dan Viet records a March 14 closure notice and a March 15 official exchange confirming clearance could not proceed. The provincial April 20 report records one inbound truck, while the later Finance Ministry letter 4612 records zero and internally conflicts between March 15 and April 15 onset dates. Government News separately reports cargo processing on April 21. These discrepancies remain visible. However, daily official trade reports dated to April 22 and April 26 explicitly record five and eight imports respectively, with no exports. Therefore some China-to-Vietnam freight clearance was restored by April 22, independently of the disputed first-shipment date. This is a partial later-access bound, not unrestricted bilateral trade, exact first reopening, or proof of a continuous March–April closure.

phases.Movement / crossing / phase scope: Myanmar–Laos Friendship Bridge at Kenglat/Tachileik–Laos
phases.Qualification:
R6-EA-007-FU1: May 13, 2022 marks restoration of conditional cargo permission at the Myanmar–Laos Friendship Bridge. The initial COVID closure date and actual first commercial passage are unknown. Only the driver and conductor were permitted at designated transfer places under vaccination and testing conditions; ordinary passenger entry and exit remained prohibited. The retrospective report supports a prolonged interruption, but not an exact total or uniform suspension of every category.

Later actual goods access: the Trade Department reports Myanmar-to-Laos aquatic and agricultural exports through Kenglat during April–July 2023, establishing some outbound commercial access by July 31, 2023 at latest. It also reports 22 tonnes of tobacco exported in the first week of September 2023 (September 1–7). The Ministry of Information published this account on September 12; that is the report date, not the movement date. Neither interval establishes the first restored cargo crossing, unrestricted bilateral trade or passenger reopening.

CNI’s January 2024 account describes a four-year closure, which conflicts with the documented May 2022 cargo permission and actual 2023 exports. Its January 25 reopening ceremony is not treated as the first cargo reopening or proof of continuous closure since 2020.

phases.Qualification:
REC50-R28-001-P1: RFA’s April 30 report describes trucks returning after ten days, and Eleven’s May 1 report explicitly gives April 20. GNLM’s May 8 retrospective gives April 11. Both concern Bridge II cargo, so the onset conflict remains visible; the matched April 30 truck return and sustained interruption support qualified visualization and greater-than-24-hour eligibility. Exact elapsed duration and imposing-side attribution remain unresolved. CNI’s May 5 combined account mentions April 21 for suspended activities at both bridges; it does not resolve the cargo-specific disagreement. Inland Asia Highway damage is separate from passage over the international bridge.

REC50-R28-001-P2: Generic April 27 reopening and travel into Myanmar alone do not establish restored Thai admission for pass holders. May reports now supply document-specific conditional access, bounded by May 6 without claiming the first Thai readmission or restoration of every booklet type. IMNA’s March 1 UID date conflicts with MOI and Eleven’s May 1 account and is not used. The official rationale for the original Thai document refusal remains unknown; later Myanmar UID policy motives are not retroactively assigned to it. February 2026 guarantor conditions are a later observation, not evidence of uninterrupted April 2024–2026 restrictions.

Refusal of temporary-border-pass and pass-booklet travel from Myanmar into Thailand at Friendship Bridge I on 21 April 2024.
Start: 2024-04-21.
Last confirmed refusal: 2024-04-21. Partial later border-pass access is reported by 2024-05-06; exact first restoration of every affected pass type is not established.

Later access for P2: a May 1 Myawady Daily summary describes temporary passes operating again after Bridge I reopened. Eleven on May 4 describes Myanmar-to-Mae Sot TBP/BP travel under the new UID requirement, and IMNA on May 6 interviews a Myawady resident who traveled to Mae Sot in that context. SC14-R1 — Announced window

Start: 2020-12-22 to 2020-12-23.
Scheduled endpoint: 2021-01-04 to 2021-01-06.

Later observations: UN Malawi still reported land borders closed on January 29, 2021; the renewal chain connecting this to the initial order is not established. phases.Qualification: SC14-R1: Malawi24 quotes immediate effect December 22; FEWS dates effect December 23. Fourteen-day schedule yields January 4–6 bounds depending on onset and inclusive/elapsed counting. These are linked alternative interpretations, not evidence of a fifteen-day order or observed reopening. Renewal chain remains unresolved. Numeric day fields must be withheld: calendar bounds represent linked counting interpretations and must not be combined by independent endpoint cross-products. The initial announcement explicitly excepted returning Malawians and essential-service providers. Later January closure and April open-border observations do not justify a single December–April interval or an exact reopening date.

phases.Qualification:
W-022-FU1: The contemporary report places Liberia’s Guinea and Côte d’Ivoire first-phase closure on 30 March 2020. It does not date the Sierra Leone phase or establish a continuous physical closure. Cargo transfers and humanitarian exceptions remained. A Liberia Revenue Authority statement dated 4 May describes the continuing passenger restrictions and cargo arrangements.

Ganta–Guinea later access: Local Voices Liberia’s report published 12 March 2021 quotes the Nimba immigration deputy commander saying the official border had reopened for travellers under health screening, alongside interviews with local traders. This supports official passenger access by that date at Ganta, not an exact first reopening day, observed first crossing, nationwide repeal or an endpoint for Côte d’Ivoire. The report also describes irregular passage during the closure.

An SSHAP March 2021 briefing reports an earlier Guinea–Liberia reopening in October 2020. The relevant passage was recovered from a transcription, but its underlying footnote and exact crossing/side could not be verified. It is not adopted as an exact endpoint or used to infer uninterrupted closure until March 2021.

IOM’s December 2021 survey describes increased movement after reopening across official and unofficial Sierra Leone border points. This is a different frontier and does not end the Guinea/Côte d’Ivoire phase. A secondary tracker’s 13 October 2021 full-land-reopening claim remains uncorroborated by the original dated FCDO advice. Other gates’ first passenger restoration and national formal repeal remain unknown; the old COVID restriction is not asserted to continue into the present.

W-022-FU1: The contemporary report places Liberia’s Guinea and Côte d’Ivoire first-phase closure on 30 March 2020. It does not date the Sierra Leone phase or establish a continuous physical closure. Cargo transfers and humanitarian exceptions remained. A Liberia Revenue Authority statement dated 4 May describes the continuing passenger restrictions and cargo arrangements.

Ganta–Guinea later access: Local Voices Liberia’s report published 12 March 2021 quotes the Nimba immigration deputy commander saying the official border had reopened for travellers under health screening, alongside interviews with local traders. This supports official passenger access by that date at Ganta, not an exact first reopening day, observed first crossing, nationwide repeal or an endpoint for Côte d’Ivoire. The report also describes irregular passage during the closure.

An SSHAP March 2021 briefing reports an earlier Guinea–Liberia reopening in October 2020. The relevant passage was recovered from a transcription, but its underlying footnote and exact crossing/side could not be verified. It is not adopted as an exact endpoint or used to infer uninterrupted closure until March 2021.

IOM’s December 2021 survey describes increased movement after reopening across official and unofficial Sierra Leone border points. This is a different frontier and does not end the Guinea/Côte d’Ivoire phase. A secondary tracker’s 13 October 2021 full-land-reopening claim remains uncorroborated by the original dated FCDO advice. Other gates’ first passenger restoration and national formal repeal remain unknown; the old COVID restriction is not asserted to continue into the present.
